cruxes.title: Execution Context & the Call Stack
cruxes.hook: You already believe nothing exists until its line runs. JS breaks that — watch it break, then find out what actually happens.
cruxes.owns: sequential execution (a prior you already own from Python)

cruxes.title: Hoisting
cruxes.hook: Why can you call a function before you 'wrote' it, but get undefined (not an error) for a variable?

cruxes.title: Scope & the Lexical Environment
cruxes.hook: How does an inner function see an outer variable it never received?
cruxes.owns: execution context has a memory space with a name (crux 1)

cruxes.title: let, const, the Temporal Dead Zone & Block Scope
cruxes.hook: let/const are hoisted too — so why does touching them early throw instead of giving undefined?

cruxes.title: Closures
cruxes.hook: A function returns, its execution context is deleted — so how does the inner function still remember its variables?

cruxes.title: First-Class Functions & Callbacks
cruxes.hook: Functions as values — you already do this in Python. What does JS add?
cruxes.owns: functions live in memory just like values (crux 1)

cruxes.title: The Event Loop & Async JS
cruxes.hook: JS has one call stack and does one thing at a time — so how does setTimeout not just freeze everything?

cruxes.title: Inside the JS Engine (V8)
cruxes.hook: Zoom out: what is physically running the execution context and call stack?
cruxes.owns: execution context & call stack (crux 1) + event loop (crux 7)

cruxes.title: Higher-Order Functions: map, filter, reduce
cruxes.hook: The payoff — build map/filter/reduce yourself from what you now know about functions and closures.
